why_ai: Unlicensed screen work on rented hardware, but AI demand itself grows the market for serving.
why_clarity: Latency and cost per token are measured instantly; kernel and capacity work stays expert craft.
why_digital: Models and requests in, tokens out over an API, bought remotely by engineering teams.

why_ai: Buyer cares only about cost per token, so any provider will do, though compute demand grows.
why_clarity: Cost per million tokens against an hours-long deadline is exact, repeated and instantly checked.
why_digital: Offline jobs submitted as data and returned as data through remote APIs.

why_ai: Long hardware commitments against bursty demand are high-stakes bets, but forecasting is well-posed for automation.
why_clarity: Utilisation at a latency guarantee is measurable, but commitment outcomes surface slowly over contract terms.
why_digital: Forecasting and allocation run on telemetry and spreadsheets inside the provider.

why_ai: Proprietary request-level cost history cannot be generated by AI and grows more valuable with demand.
why_clarity: Structured logs across millions of requests give repeatable, checkable cost models.
why_digital: Request logs in, empirical cost accounts out, entirely as data.

why_ai: Accounts follow measured latency, not people; batching decisions are optimisable while serving demand grows.
why_clarity: Time-to-first-token and inter-token latency are exact metrics checked on every request.
why_digital: User prompts in, streamed tokens out, all through remote endpoints.

why_ai: Each new architecture on each accelerator is novel expert work, though search-based compilers are closing in.
why_clarity: Near-peak efficiency is benchmarked instantly, but the hand-tuning method differs by engineer and release.
why_digital: Model code and kernels are tuned on screens and shipped as software.

why_ai: Commodity endpoint product with no licence, but AI adoption keeps growing serving demand.
why_clarity: Endpoints serve millions of near-identical requests with latency and throughput measured continuously.
why_digital: An API endpoint bought and consumed remotely by product and data teams.

why_ai: Isolating tenants on hardware not built for sharing is hard, adversarial systems work that AI will not commoditise.
why_clarity: Cross-tenant latency interference is measurable, but enforcement methods are still being invented.
why_digital: Platform engineering on schedulers and memory partitions, delivered as software behaviour.

why_ai: Comparing quantised and full-precision output on a customer's task is a mechanical measurement software runs.
why_clarity: Quality loss on a defined task is measured directly by comparing outputs.
why_digital: Model outputs and task data in, quality accounts out.

why_ai: Choosing which customer to degrade is a pressured commercial call, but the policy is expressible in code.
why_clarity: Arbitration is ad hoc with incomplete contract information and outcomes judged after the incident.
why_digital: Engineers act on dashboards and schedulers; nothing physical is touched.

why_ai: Bisecting versioned layers to find a regression is mechanical and largely automatable by 2031.
why_clarity: Bisection is a known method and the fix is verified instantly by rerunning the benchmark.
why_digital: Version history and benchmarks in, attributed regressions out, all on screens.
